source.title: Principled Steering via Null-space Projection for Jailbreak Defense in Vision-Language Models
source.authors: Xingyu Zhu; Beier Zhu; Shuo Wang; Junfeng Fang; Kesen Zhao; Hanwang Zhang; Xiangnan He

record.file_problem: None apparent; the paper and supplementary material are present. Some table formatting is flattened.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses activation steering and refusal-oriented representations to build a VLM jailbreak defense, but evaluates its own null-space-projected method rather than testing the claimed single difference-in-means direction.
record.gate_note: The paper defines a refusal-versus-compliance mean-difference direction as background, but does not report a direct ablation or addition test of that direction. It does not test the claimed weight edit or whether jailbreaks suppress the claimed direction. The chosen steering layers and other setup choices are not outcome rows.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes NullSteer, a learned null-space-projected steering defense for VLMs. It reports only its own method's toxicity, ASR and utility against baselines. It never ablates or adds the harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction to test whether that direction mediates refusal. The mean-difference refusal direction (Eq. 3) appears only as background.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that NullSteer improves VLM robustness to perturbation-based and adaptive jailbreaks while preserving benign utility, and they attribute this to restricting steering to the null space of benign activations.
record.recipe_differences: The method is a learned null-space-projected transformation, targeted using refusal activations and attribution-based harmful directions. It is not the original single-direction projection ablation/addition procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper varies perturbation strength, attack setting, steering strength, and numbers of benign and malicious activations; it reports that these choices affect results. The steering layer is set to 20 for 13B models and 14 for the 7B model.

fits_no_version.finding: NullSteer, a learned null-space-projected steering method, gives the lowest toxicity and ASR among the compared defenses on MiniGPT-4, Qwen2-VL and LLaVA-v1.5 under PGD visual attacks. MM-Vet, MMBench and XSTest scores stay near vanilla.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Null-space-constrained learned refusal steering reduces visual-jailbreak outputs in VLMs without a measured loss on benign benchmarks.

record.problems: The reported outcomes evaluate the authors' own induced defense, not the claimed single direction. The text gives no uncertainty estimates. Some table and figure values are flattened or figure-only, and the main experiments use three VLMs and a limited set of attack benchmarks.
record.rows_left_out: Other per-model/per-attack table entries, OOD attack results, and figure sweeps are not catalogued here; the table extraction is flattened and the study's own defense outcomes do not directly test any listed claim version.

untested.parts: No ablation or addition test of a single difference-in-means refusal direction, and no capability check of such an intervention. The Refusal Pairs (CAA) baseline appears only as a comparison method. The over-refusal claim for plain steering in Fig. 1 has no rates.
Visual jailbreaks are defended against, but there is no analysis of whether they suppress the refusal direction, and no training against ablation.
No comparison of single, affine, cone or multi-direction accounts.
No separation of harm judgment from refusal.
Transfer is across attack types and perturbation levels, not across languages, model variants or base-to-instruct.

record.verdict_notes: All rows rightly carry versions ["none"]; they are the study's own method compared with baselines. Table 1 includes a Refusal Pairs (CAA-style mean-difference refusal steering) baseline that lowers ASR versus no defense, e.g. MiniGPT-4 unconstrained 53.64% to 16.36%. This is a baseline comparison, not a designed test of V1, so no verdict is given. The paper also gives no utility or over-refusal numbers for that baseline. No uncertainty is reported. The model set is three VLMs with a small PGD test set of 30 adversarial images.

versions.untested_parts: No direct test of ablating or adding a single harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction, or of its effect on general capability.
The attacks evaluated are visual jailbreak attacks, not tests of whether attacks suppress the claimed direction; no training against its ablation.
No comparison of single-direction, affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts of refusal.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No test of transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models. The paper evaluates defense generalization across attack settings, which is not this version's transfer claim.
No comparison of refusal training methods or training stages.
